Standard deviational ellipse

Source: R/sp.R
sdell.Rd

The ellipse whose axes lie along the eigenvectors of the weighted covariance matrix of the points about their mean centre, with semi-axes c times the square roots of its eigenvalues (Wang, Shi and Miao 2015). It is the ellipse of the rotated-axes formulas of Lefever (1926) and Ebdon (1988) once the same divisor is used; texts differ only in the divisor (k) and in the multiplier (some multiply by sqrt(2)). The curve of the standard deviation by direction that Lefever drew is not this ellipse (Gong 2002); the ellipse is returned. For bivariate normal points the ellipse with c = sqrt(-2 * log(1 - p)) covers a share p of them: c = 1 covers 39.3 per cent, c = 2 86.5 per cent. The parallel-axis identity behind the ellipse's centre is proved in Lean: see proof("sdell").

Usage

sdell(x, y = NULL, w = NULL, k = 1, c = 1, lonlat = FALSE)

Arguments

x, y

The points: x and y numeric vectors of equal length; or x a matrix or data frame with columns named x and y (or X and Y, as sf::st_coordinates() names them, or lon and lat with lonlat = TRUE) and y NULL; or x an sf or sfc object of POINT geometries, whose coordinate reference system must agree with lonlat. An unnamed two-column matrix is read as x then y; other columns are never taken by position. Vectors given separately (x, y, and w or t where a function takes them) are matched by name when every one is named and no name repeats, as elsewhere in the package; otherwise by position. No missing or infinite values.

w

NULL for equal weights, or one non-negative weight per point (counts at a location, say), with a positive sum.

k

The divisor offset: 0, 1 or 2; the total weight must exceed it.

c

The multiplier of the standard deviations: one positive number.

lonlat

FALSE (the default) when x and y are planar coordinates in one length unit; TRUE when they are longitude and latitude in degrees, which are then projected to metres by eqproj() about their own centre, and centres are returned in degrees. It is never guessed.

Value

A named numeric vector: mx, my (the mean centre, in degrees when lonlat = TRUE), a and b (the semi-major and semi-minor axes, a >= b, in the unit of the coordinates or metres), angle (of the major axis, in radians anticlockwise from the x axis (east), in [0, pi); 0 when a == b) and area (pi * a * b).

References

Wang, B., Shi, W. and Miao, Z. (2015). Confidence analysis of standard deviational ellipse and its extension into higher dimensional Euclidean space. PLoS ONE, 10(3), e0118537. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0118537

Gong, J. (2002). Clarifying the standard deviational ellipse. Geographical Analysis, 34(2), 155-167. doi:10.1111/j.1538-4632.2002.tb01082.x

Examples

set.seed(2)
x <- rnorm(200)
sdell(x, 0.5 * x + rnorm(200, sd = 0.3), c = 2)
#>            mx            my             a             b         angle 
#> -0.0007417526  0.0681841044  2.4146550213  0.5262845280  0.4870207069 
#>          area 
#>  3.9923220528
